page.notesHint: Free text for your team: what is this server for, who is responsible, links (https://…) become clickable.

agents.intro: Agents report other servers to X-TOOLS – outbound only, they never receive commands. Install one on the Proxmox host and one on every LXC/VM that runs Docker.
agents.name: Name
agents.keyOnce: Copy the key now – it is shown only once. Only a hash is stored.
agents.step4: Behind Cloudflare Access: add a service token and a “Service Auth” rule for /api/agent/report (see Help).
agents.proxmoxHint: Also report nodes, storage, LXCs and VMs through the Proxmox API (read-only).
agents.proxmoxUrlHint: Seen from the Proxmox host – usually https://127.0.0.1:8006
agents.verifyTls: Verify the TLS certificate (off for the default self-signed certificate)
agents.proxmoxHowto: Proxmox: Datacenter → Permissions → API Tokens → Add; then Permissions → Add → API Token Permission, path /, role PVEAuditor (read-only). For control use a role with VM.PowerMgmt, VM.Config.* and Datastore.AllocateSpace – docs/agents.md has a ready pveum command. The token is stored encrypted, so the next install command is filled in.
agents.cfHint: Service token so the agent gets through (rule: Service Auth for /api/agent/).
agents.composeRootsHint: Where to look for compose files on that server (comma-separated)
agents.reinstallNote: This creates a new key. The agent installed so far stops reporting until you run the new command.
agents.runThis: Run this on the server, as root
agents.runThisHint: On Proxmox you are root in the shell; elsewhere replace “| sh” with “| sudo sh”.
agents.fact1: Works once and only for one hour.
agents.fact2: Installs the systemd service x-tools-agent (Python 3.10+, nothing else) – read-only, no open ports.
agents.fact3: The server shows up on the Proxmox or Docker page within a minute.
agents.dockerAltHint: Use deploy/agent from the repository with this .env (the key is shown only now):

kinds.proxmoxHint: Host metrics, nodes, storage and all LXCs/VMs via the Proxmox API (read-only token).
kinds.dockerHint: A server, LXC or VM with Docker: containers, compose files, git status.
kinds.linuxHint: Any Linux server, VM or LXC: load, memory, disks, systemd services, open ports, updates. Optionally Docker as well.

agents.removedText: X-TOOLS no longer accepts reports from this agent. To remove it from {{host}} as well, run this there:
agents.uninstallHint: Removes the systemd service and its files, or the Docker container – whichever is installed.
agents.uninstallNote: Without it the agent keeps trying to report and is rejected. Later you can also find the command under Help → Agents.
agents.updateHint: A newer agent is available: create a new install command and run it on the server.
agents.controlHintDocker: Operators can start, stop and restart containers on this server and read their logs. Off: the agent only reports.
agents.controlHintProxmox: Operators can start, shut down, stop and reboot LXCs/VMs, change CPU, memory, swap, start at boot and tags, and grow disks. The API token needs the matching privileges (see the hint above).
agents.secretStored: Stored – leave empty to keep it
agents.prefilled: Filled in from the last install command. Stored secrets are kept unless you enter new ones.
agents.controlHintLinux: Operators can start, stop and restart systemd services, read their logs and reboot the server. The agent runs as root. Off: the agent only reports.
agents.alsoDockerHint: This server runs Docker: its containers appear on the Docker page.

about.keyEnv: The secret key comes from XT_SECRET_KEY – keep a copy of it.
about.keyFile: The secret key is stored in {{dir}}/secret.key.
about.backupHint: Back up the whole data volume including the key. Without it stored credentials and tokens cannot be decrypted.
about.config: These values are set through environment variables (deploy/.env).
about.vibeText: X-TOOLS was written entirely with an AI assistant (Claude), directed by one person. It has tests and a security design, but no independent code review or security audit. Keep backups, and be careful with exposing it to the internet or giving it control over systems you care about.

general.customersHint: For sites you host for others: contacts, agreements and external checks of their domains. Stored customers are kept when you switch it off.

fleet.noData: No data in the last report.
fleet.askAdmin: Ask an admin to set up an agent.
fleet.proxmoxEmptyText: Install the X-TOOLS agent on your Proxmox host (Administration → Agents → Add server → Proxmox host). It shows nodes, storage, all LXCs and VMs with their configuration – outbound only, no open ports.
fleet.dockerEmptyText: Containers of this server come from the collector container x-tools-collector (started by setup.sh). For other servers, LXCs or VMs with Docker install an agent (Administration → Agents → Add server → Docker host).
fleet.pending: created, but has not reported yet
fleet.linuxEmptyText: Install the X-TOOLS agent on any Linux server, VM or LXC (Administration → Agents → Add server → Linux server). It shows load, memory, disks, systemd services, open ports and pending updates – outbound only, no open ports.

account.changed: Password changed – other sessions were logged out.
account.twoFactorText: Besides your password, log in with a code from an authenticator app (e.g. Apple Passwords, 1Password, Google Authenticator, Aegis).
account.step1: Scan the QR code with your authenticator app (or enter the key manually).
account.step2: Enter the 6-digit code it shows to confirm.
account.qrAlt: QR code for the authenticator app
account.recoveryText: Store these codes somewhere safe (e.g. your password manager). Each one logs you in once if you lose your phone. They are shown only now.
account.languageText: Language of the interface. Problem texts and notifications from the server stay in English for now.

backup.createText: Database and secret key in one file, encrypted with a passphrase you choose. Anyone with file and passphrase can read everything in it, including credentials.
backup.passphraseHint: At least 10 characters – without it the backup cannot be restored.
backup.restoreText: Replaces everything in this installation with the backup. Everyone is logged out afterwards.
backup.confirmText: All current data is replaced by {{name}}. This cannot be undone.

users.intro: Who may log in and what they may do.

users.initialPasswordHint: Tell it to the user – they can change it under Settings → Account.

audit.intro: Who did what – kept for one year.

deploy.title: Websites
deploy.empty: No websites deployed from git yet. Add one to roll out a customer's website with a single click.
deploy.noDeployer: The deployer is not running, so nothing can be rolled out. Enable it with COMPOSE_PROFILES=deploy in deploy/.env and run setup.sh again (see Installation → Deploying customer websites).
deploy.name: Name
deploy.repoHint: https:// address of the git repository. A private repository needs an access token below.
deploy.portHint: Without a compose file in the repository, a folder with index.html is served by nginx on this port of 127.0.0.1 – put your proxy or tunnel in front of it.
deploy.tokenHint: Only for private repositories (e.g. a read-only deploy token). Stored encrypted, never shown again.
deploy.envHint: Written to the .env file of the website on every deploy, e.g. database passwords. Stored encrypted.

linux.noSystemd: systemd is not available on this server.

maintenance.title: Pause alerts
maintenance.text: During maintenance nothing is sent. Problems stay visible, marked as paused, and no “back to normal” message follows. If a problem is still there when the time is up, you are told after the usual delay.

jobs.empty: No jobs yet. Add a cron job or backup script: it calls a secret address when it has run, and X-TOOLS alerts you when the call stays away.
jobs.name: Name
jobs.expectedHint: How often the job should report.
jobs.graceHint: How long after the expected time X-TOOLS waits before it raises the alarm.
jobs.howto: Call this address at the end of the job. Anyone with the address can report for the job, so keep it secret.
jobs.howtoSimple: At the end of a script
jobs.newTokenConfirm: The old address stops working. Continue?
jobs.accessHint: Behind Cloudflare Access? The path /api/heartbeat/ needs a bypass rule, otherwise the job gets a login page.

autobackup.title: Automatic backup
autobackup.enableHint: Creates the encrypted backup on a schedule and writes it to the locations below.
autobackup.keepHint: The newest N files stay in a folder, older ones are deleted. WebDAV: upload only.
autobackup.passphraseHint: Needed to encrypt the files. It is stored encrypted in X-TOOLS so the job can run without you.
autobackup.passphraseSaved: Saved. Enter a new one only to change it. Keep it safe – without it a backup cannot be restored.
autobackup.locationsHint: Folder: must be writable inside the container (mount a volume). The default folder lies in the data volume – a copy on another machine is safer. WebDAV: Nextcloud and others.
autobackup.name: Name
